subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing for Acme — GPU pool recommendation and commit options
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Date: 2025-11-12 09:12 PST
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial workload details and ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — Acme is moving a production workload to a dedicated inference pool and we need Redwood's recommendation on pool sizing, pricing, and commit options. High level info below:

- Expected steady-state: ~150,000 requests/day (roughly 1.7 requests/sec avg).
- Average request: ~1,200 tokens (prompt + expected generations).
- Long-context profile: ~15% of requests exceed 10k tokens; those can go up to ~20k tokens.
- Concurrency: steady 40 concurrent requests, peaks up to ~90 concurrent during business hours.
- SLOs: 95th latency target for generation under 250ms for standard requests; we can tolerate higher for the long-context ones but want a clear throughput guarantee.
- Timeline: want dedicated pool by end of Jan; evaluating 12-month reserved commit.

Can you confirm what GPU pool size you'd recommend (and autoscale headroom), expected tokens/sec throughput, and a ballpark for committed pricing + discount tiers? Procurement is looped on this thread. I've attached a small traffic sample (traffic_sample.csv) — call out anything else you need.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Corp

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Date: 2025-11-12 10:30 PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial workload details and ask

Hi Sarah — thanks for the details and the sample. Quick follow-ups so we size this right:

1) Of the 15% long-context requests, are they read-heavy (large prompt only) or do they also require long generation?
2) Peak burst duration — are those 90-concurrency spikes for ~minutes or sustained (~hours)?
3) Which model family do you plan to serve (open Llama-style, 70B dense, MPT, or a quantized variant)? That materially affects memory and per-GPU throughput.

Prelim guidance: with ~40 steady concurrency and 15% long-context, customers typically land in the 6–10 GPU pool range for H100-class hardware with autoscale to cover short peaks. For 12-month reserved commits we offer a pricing ladder: 10–20% off list depending on commit size, with additional incremental discounts for multi-year/enterprise terms.

If you can confirm the three items above I’ll send a concrete GPU pool proposal + pricing matrix and a SOW draft.

Best,
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-11-13 15:05 PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial workload details and ask

Hi Karthik — answers below and attached the traffic_sample.csv you asked for.

- The 15% long-context requests are ~80% read-heavy (large prompt / retrieval-style) and ~20% require long generation (continuations up to ~5k tokens generated).
- Peaks are bursty but can be sustained for 30–90 minutes during certain batch windows.
- We're planning to run a quantized 70B family (8-bit or 4-bit depending on trade-offs). We'll validate quality during a pilot.

Procurement note: we prefer an annual reserved commit; please include both an annual and monthly overage option in the proposal.

Thanks,
Sarah

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-14 09:45 PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial workload details and ask

Sarah / Tom — based on the sample and your answers, here's a recommended configuration and commercial starting point. Inline summary first; attached SOW + pricing sheet for line items.

--- Technical recommendation ---
- Model: quantized 70B (4-bit where acceptable; fall back to 8-bit for higher quality segments).
- GPU pool: baseline 8x H100-80GB equivalent GPUs (we size for steady-state concurrency of 40 with the 15% long-context included).
- Autoscale: allow autoscale to 12 GPUs for sustained bursts up to 90 concurrency. Autoscale policy: scaling buffer of 20% headroom for queue spikes.
- Throughput estimate: baseline pool (8 GPUs) achieves ~220k tokens/sec aggregate (model & quantization dependent) — sufficient for your steady traffic plus margin; autoscaled 12 GPU pool ~330k tokens/sec.
- Long-context handling: enable prefix KV cache for the read-heavy long-context requests to reduce compute for repeated context; for long-generation long-context requests we recommend a separate queue priority and a small dedicated GPU reserve (1 GPU) to avoid head-of-line blocking.

--- Commercial / pricing ---
- List price baseline (monthly equivalent): $85k/mo for 8-GPU baseline (includes infra + Redwood managed runtime).
- 12-month reserved commit pricing: 18% standard discount off list for a 12-month commit at this scale.
- Accelerator discount tiers: 22% for >$500k ARR commit; 25% for multi-year.
- Autoscale overage: monthly overage billed at 1.15x the pro-rated list rate for additional GPU-hours beyond the reserved commit.
- SLA: 99.5% availability for the dedicated pool; throughput guarantees tied to nominal GPU count (we will quantify tokens/sec in SOW appendix).

Attachments: Acme_Dedicated_SOW_v1.pdf, RDW_pricing_sheet_ACME_v2.xlsx

Next steps: if the technical sizing and pricing look reasonable, we can: (a) lock in a 12-month commit at the 18% discount and start pilot infra provisioning (non-production) within 3 weeks, (b) finalize SOW and routing/policy details, and (c) sign DocuSign.

If you'd like a more aggressive commercial, I can loop finance/ops for an approved discount special.

Best,
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-15 11:20 PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — internal pricing alignment (Acme)

Karthik / Laura — quick internal note before we finalize the external SOW:

- Technical: 8->12 GPU baseline is reasonable. Suggest ensuring the SOW explicitly calls out the KV cache behavior and the 1 GPU reserved for long-generation to prevent HOF issues (call this the "long-gen isolate"). Also require a 14-day notice for any capacity scale-downs on our side.
- Commercial: instead of 18% flat for 12 months, propose an 18% baseline with a one-time onboarding credit (1 month free) for a 12-month commit, or trade a 20% discount for a $100k minimum ARR guarantee. Overages: cap the effective overage multiplier at 1.25x for the first 3 months.
- Approval: Laura, can you confirm finance tolerance for a 20% band in exchange for the ARR floor? If yes, I recommend offering 20% + 1-month credit to close.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-11-18 09:06 PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing & pricing for Acme (next steps)

Karthik — thanks for the clear recommendation. Quick responses and a small request from procurement:

- We can proceed with the 8-GPU baseline + autoscale to 12 for peaks. Please include the "long-gen isolate" (1 GPU) and the KV cache behavior in the SOW appendix.
- Commercial: procurement is asking for a 15% discount on top of the 12-month reserved pricing you quoted (effectively asking for 33% off list relative to the example). If that's a non-starter, we'd accept your 18% + 1-month onboarding credit suggestion.
- We need explicit throughput guarantees in the SOW (tokens/sec at baseline and autoscale levels) and an SLA clause for capacity transition timing during scale events.

If you can send the updated SOW with the 18% + 1-month credit option and the tokens/sec appendix, we can route to DocuSign and aim to sign within the week.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Corp
